# m00 — Slip-and-Fall at Greenmarket Foods (test fixture)

Marisol Ondrejka, age 52, is a home health aide who lives in Halden County. On the
evening of Friday, February 14, 2025, she stopped at the Greenmarket Foods store on
Larkspur Avenue after her shift to pick up groceries [m00.fact.001]. As she turned
into the produce aisle at around 6:00 p.m., she slipped on a wet patch on the floor
and fell hard, landing on her right side [m00.fact.002]. She had been looking at her
phone, texting her daughter, in the moment just before she turned the corner
[m00.fact.003].

Ondrejka came down on her right wrist and right knee. The wrist swelled immediately
and she could not put weight on the knee without sharp pain [m00.fact.004]. There was
no wet-floor cone, sign, or any other warning anywhere near the spill [m00.fact.005].
She did not see what the liquid was — it could have been water from the misters over
the produce, or something oilier that had leaked from a container; she genuinely never
got a clear look at it [m00.fact.006].

For what she recalls as several long minutes, no store employee came to help her; other
shoppers eventually stopped and one helped her to a bench near the registers
[m00.fact.007]. When a store employee finally arrived, that employee said, in passing,
that they had "been meaning to get to that spill" — Ondrejka took this to mean the store
knew the floor was wet before she fell [m00.fact.008]. A manager filled out an in-store
incident report that evening and took down Ondrejka's name and phone number; Ondrejka
was not given a copy [m00.fact.009]. She does not know whether the store has security-
camera video of the aisle or of her fall [m00.fact.010].

That same night, Ondrejka's daughter drove her to an urgent-care clinic, where staff
X-rayed the wrist, diagnosed a sprain and a possible small fracture, fitted her with a
wrist brace, and told her to follow up if the pain did not improve [m00.fact.011]. Six
weeks later she was still wearing the brace on and off and still could not grip firmly
with her right hand [m00.fact.012].

The injury has hit Ondrejka's livelihood directly. Her work as a home health aide
requires lifting and transferring patients, which she cannot safely do with an injured
wrist and knee; she has been afraid to return to work and afraid of what missing the
income will do to her [m00.fact.013]. She has not told many people how frightened she is
about the money and about whether she will get her strength back.

Ondrejka has been through injury claims before. In 2022 she was rear-ended in a car
accident and made an insurance claim, and a few years before that she filed a workers'
compensation claim after hurting her back on the job [m00.fact.014]. She is uneasy about
these prior claims coming up, worried that a lawyer — or the store — will think she is
the kind of person who is always looking to sue [m00.fact.015].

## Timeline (test fixture)

- Fri, Feb 14, 2025, ~6:00 p.m. — Slip and fall in the produce aisle at Greenmarket
  Foods; incident report taken that evening; urgent-care visit that night.
- Late Mar 2025 — Still symptomatic; brace still in use; not back at work.
- as_of (fixture) — Ondrejka is seeking a lawyer's help.
